skill.name: multi-stage-dockerfile
skill.description: Create optimized multi-stage Dockerfiles for any language or framework
skill.summary: Design multi-stage Dockerfiles with lean runtime images, efficient layer caching, and container security practices.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: All seven static findings are false positives involving Markdown code spans or defensive Docker guidance. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious execution in SKILL.md. The skill provides instructions, not executable tooling or verified security guarantees.

static_findings.snippet: - Use meaningful stage names with the `AS` keyword (e.g., `FROM node:18 AS builder`)
- Specify exact version tags to ensure reproducible builds (e.g., `python:3.11-slim` not just `pytho
- Use `.dockerignore` to prevent unnecessary files from being included in the build context
- Combine related RUN commands with `&&` to reduce layer count
- Avoid running containers as root - use `USER` instruction to specify a non-root user
- Avoid running containers as root - use `USER` instruction to specify a non-root user
- Use multi-stage builds to avoid including build secrets in the final image

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 13 uses Markdown backticks to format the AS keyword and a Dockerfile stage example. These code spans do not execute shell or Ruby commands.
Line 19 formats container image tags with Markdown backticks while recommending explicit versions. It contains no shell substitution or executable Ruby expression.
Line 28 formats the .dockerignore filename as inline code and recommends limiting the build context. The backticks are Markdown syntax, not command execution.
Line 29 discusses combining Dockerfile RUN commands and formats the && operator with Markdown backticks. It supplies no malicious command or untrusted input execution.
Line 34 formats the Dockerfile USER instruction with Markdown backticks. The recommendation reduces runtime privileges and does not execute a command.
Line 34 recommends selecting a non-root container user through the Dockerfile USER instruction. It does not enumerate host accounts or collect system information.
Line 38 recommends keeping build secrets out of the final image. It does not request secret discovery, host inspection, or transmission of sensitive data.

content.value_statement: Container images can retain unnecessary build tools and rebuild dependencies too often. This skill guides Dockerfile design with separate build stages, efficient caching, and minimal runtime dependencies.
actual_capabilities: Guide separation of dependency, build, test, and runtime stages with meaningful names.
Recommend copying only required build artifacts into the runtime image.
Suggest official minimal, distroless, or Alpine base images according to application compatibility.
Guide layer ordering and build context exclusions to improve caching.
Recommend non-root users, restrictive permissions, and removal of unnecessary runtime packages.
Suggest runtime environment settings and application-appropriate health checks.
limitations: Provides written guidance without bundled scripts, automated builds, or vulnerability scanners.
Requires project-specific build commands, dependency details, and runtime requirements.
Does not guarantee smaller images, faster builds, or vulnerability-free results without testing.
Version tags are mutable, and separate stages alone do not protect secrets in build caches or intermediate layers.

use_cases.title: Containerize an Application
use_cases.description: Create separate build and runtime stages while preserving the dependencies and startup behavior an application needs.

use_cases.title: Improve CI Build Efficiency
use_cases.description: Review dependency installation order and build context contents to reduce avoidable cache invalidation.

use_cases.title: Review Runtime Image Hardening
use_cases.description: Assess runtime users, file permissions, base image choices, and unnecessary packages before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Multi-Stage Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multi-stage Dockerfile for my [language and framework] application. Ask for missing build commands, startup commands, and runtime requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Separate Build and Runtime Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Dockerfile and separate build dependencies from runtime requirements. Explain which artifacts must be copied and which tools can be excluded.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Build Caching
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Dockerfile and project structure for caching improvements. Suggest layer ordering and build context exclusions, then explain how to test the changes.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my multi-stage Dockerfile for production deployment. Evaluate base image compatibility, non-root permissions, artifact selection, runtime environment settings, and health checks. Identify assumptions requiring verification.

output_examples.input: Review a Node.js image that includes build tools and development dependencies at runtime.
output: Use a builder stage to install dependencies and compile the application.
Keep only production dependencies and required application artifacts in the runtime stage.
Select a non-root runtime user and verify access to required files.
Test application startup before comparing final image sizes.

output_examples.input: Dependency installation repeats whenever application source files change.
output: Copy dependency manifests before application source files.
Install dependencies in an earlier layer to preserve its cache when only source files change.
Exclude unnecessary files from the build context.
Compare successive builds to verify cache reuse.

best_practices: Provide build commands, startup requirements, and native dependency constraints before requesting a Dockerfile.
Build and test the final image, including health checks and non-root file access.
Use image digests for immutable references and secret mounts for sensitive build credentials.
anti_patterns: Copying the entire builder filesystem into the runtime image.
Choosing Alpine or distroless images without checking dependency and health check compatibility.
Assuming separate build stages automatically remove secrets from intermediate layers and build caches.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it support my language or framework?
faq.answer: Its guidance is language-independent. You must supply the build process, runtime requirements, and compatibility constraints for your project.

faq.question: Does this skill build or scan images automatically?
faq.answer: No. It contains written guidance and recommends vulnerability scanning, but includes no build automation or scanner.

faq.question: Will a multi-stage build always make my image smaller?
faq.answer: No. Size depends on base images, runtime dependencies, and copied artifacts. Measure the resulting image after testing.

faq.question: Do explicit version tags guarantee reproducible builds?
faq.answer: No. Tags can change. Use image digests and locked dependencies when you need stronger reproducibility.

faq.question: Are build secrets safe in a separate builder stage?
faq.answer: Not automatically. Secrets can remain in intermediate layers or caches. Use build secret mounts and avoid embedding credentials in image instructions.
